title: How to Make a Shaken Raspberry Rickey for a Baby Shower

html:
When you’re planning a baby shower, a bright, bubbly drink can set the tone for celebration without overwhelming the palate. A shaken raspberry rickey shaker recipe hits that sweet‑spot: it’s light, festive, and easy to make in batches. Using a quality Cocktail Shaker Set ensures every sip is perfectly mixed and free of ice shards, giving guests a polished cocktail experience right at home.

Why Choose a Raspberry Rickey for a Baby Shower?

Raspberry rickeys are essentially a gin‑based highball with fresh raspberry puree, lime juice, and club soda. The drink’s crisp acidity balances the fruit’s natural sweetness, making it a crowd‑pleaser for both adults and designated drivers who might prefer a non‑alcoholic version. The vibrant pink hue also matches many baby shower palettes, from pastel pinks to gender‑neutral neutrals.

Essential Tools: The Cocktail Shaker Set

The only tool you truly need to nail this recipe is a reliable Cocktail Shaker Set. The set includes a stainless‑steel shaker, a double‑jigger, and a fine‑mesh strainer—all leak‑proof and designed for bar‑quality results. When you shake the raspberry puree and lime juice with ice, the set’s tight seal prevents dilution and keeps the flavor concentrated. After shaking, the built‑in strainer ensures a smooth pour, leaving any raspberry seeds behind.

Ingredients (Makes 8 Servings)

  • 2 cups fresh raspberries (plus extra for garnish)
  • 8 oz gin (or vodka for a milder profile)
  • 1/2 cup freshly squeezed lime juice (about 4 limes)
  • 1/4 cup simple syrup (adjust to taste)
  • Ice cubes
  • Club soda, chilled
  • Fresh mint leaves (optional, for garnish)

Step‑by‑Step: Creating the Perfect Shaken Raspberry Rickey

1. Prep the raspberry puree. Place the fresh raspberries in a blender and pulse until smooth. Strain the puree through a fine‑mesh sieve into a bowl to remove seeds. You’ll end up with about 1 cup of smooth raspberry juice.

2. Measure the spirits. Using the double‑jigger from your Cocktail Shaker Set, measure 8 oz of gin and add it to the shaker. If you prefer a lighter flavor, swap gin for vodka.

3. Add the citrus and sweetener. Pour the freshly squeezed lime juice and simple syrup into the shaker. The acidity of lime brightens the raspberry, while the syrup balances the tartness.

4. Combine with ice. Fill the shaker three‑quarters full with ice cubes. Secure the lid tightly—this is where the leak‑proof design of the Cocktail Shaker Set shines.

5. Shake vigorously. Hold the shaker with both hands and shake for about 12–15 seconds. You’ll feel the temperature drop and hear the rhythmic clink of ice. The goal is to chill the mixture without over‑diluting.

6. Strain and serve. Using the built‑in strainer, pour the shaken mixture into tall glasses, leaving the ice behind. Top each glass with 2–3 oz of chilled club soda for that signature fizz.

7. Garnish. Add a few whole raspberries and a sprig of mint to each glass. The garnish not only looks appealing but also adds a subtle aroma that enhances the drinking experience.

Tips for Scaling Up or Going Non‑Alcoholic

If you’re expecting a larger crowd, simply multiply the ingredient amounts and shake in two batches. For a mocktail version, replace the gin with an equal amount of sparkling water or a light herbal tea, and follow the same shaking process. The same Cocktail Shaker Set works equally well for alcoholic and non‑alcoholic mixes, making it a versatile addition to any kitchen bar.

Storing Leftover Raspberry Puree

Raspberry puree can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to three days. Keep it separate from the soda to preserve carbonation. If you need it longer, freeze the puree in ice‑cube trays and thaw as needed—this also gives you pre‑measured portions for future cocktails.

Serving Ideas and Presentation

Pair the shaken raspberry rickey with light finger foods like cucumber sandwiches, mini quiches, or fruit‑topped cupcakes. The drink’s acidity cuts through richer bites, keeping the palate refreshed. For a themed presentation, consider using pastel pink paper straws or glassware with gold rims to elevate the visual impact.

FAQ

Can I use frozen raspberries instead of fresh?

Yes. Thaw the frozen berries, then blend and strain as you would with fresh fruit. The flavor may be slightly less vibrant, so you might add a touch more simple syrup.

What’s the best way to keep the drink fizzy when serving a crowd?

Prepare the shaken raspberry‑lime mixture in advance and keep it chilled. Add club soda to each glass right before serving to maintain maximum effervescence.

Is the Cocktail Shaker Set dishwasher safe?

The stainless‑steel components are dishwasher safe, but hand‑washing the shaker and strainer prolongs their shine and ensures the seal remains airtight.
